symptom: TMS-001 could not be inserted into soa_memory.canonical_memory because postgres_projection mapped a historical checkpoint identifier into supersedes_memory_id, whose foreign key requires an existing canonical-memory row.
root_cause: The projection treated every previous_snapshot_id as a persisted Trusted Memory predecessor even when the historical predecessor was a continuity checkpoint rather than a TMS record.
early_signals: TMS-001 previous_snapshot_id uses the CHK- prefix
TMS-002 correctly references a TMS- predecessor while TMS-001 does not
human_cost: No operator troubleshooting required; ephemeral PostgreSQL CI exposed the mismatch during autonomous closure.
prevention_rule: Only map a predecessor into supersedes_memory_id when it identifies a persisted Trusted Memory snapshot; preserve non-memory historical predecessors as metadata rather than fabricating a foreign-key relationship.
automated_detection: Regression tests assert TMS-001 has no canonical-memory supersedes FK, preserves its checkpoint predecessor as metadata, and TMS-002 supersedes TMS-001.
